Lessons.Title: Problems about Fractional Measurement Data
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will solve problems using information presented in line plots.
Key idea: Line plots of fractional measurement data support comparison, addition and subtraction of measured lengths.
How to reason: Read tick labels in eighth-inches, count the marks at each value, and use like units in every comparison.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Shoe Sizes (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1: Shoe Lengths (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as 9, \(9\frac{1}{8}\), \(8\frac{6}{8}\), \(7\frac{6}{8}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2: Larger Shoes, Anyone? (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{5}{4}\), \(\frac{7}{8}\), \(\frac{3}{4}\), \(\frac{1}{2}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
Original source Cool-down is access-restricted/unverified; Edulytics substitutes goal-aligned independently authored teacher-reviewed exit prompt.
Edulytics worked model: How much longer is 9 and 1/8 inches than 8 and 6/8 inches?. Explain every transformation and check using equal wholes/units.
Open reflection: Original shoe-size table and completed line plot require teacher-verified plotted frequencies.
Original source graphics, line plots, grids or physical models are not duplicated: use teacher-provided originals/first-party teacher-approved equivalents.
